questions: Is the main reason for your visit today related to your arms or shoulders?
Do you have pain in your shoulders?
Do you have weakness in your arms?
Can you lower your arms all the way down to your sides?
Have you had any injury to your arms or shoulders?
Do you have any pain in your neck?
Do you have any numbness or tingling in your arms or hands?
Do you have any difficulty walking or with balance?
Do you have double vision, drooping eyelids, or trouble swallowing?
Do you have any skin rash or have you noticed any muscle wasting?
orders: Observe the patient's gait as they walk across the room, including turning
Test for myotonia by having the patient grip my hand tightly and then release quickly, timing the relaxation
Test for percussion myotonia by tapping the thenar eminence with a reflex hammer
Assess for resting tremor and cogwheel rigidity at the wrists and elbows during passive movement
Test for bradykinesia with rapid alternating hand movements (finger tapping, hand opening/closing)
Test postural stability with the pull test
Assess cerebellar coordination with finger-to-nose and heel-to-shin testing
Examine the tongue for fasciculations and percussion myotonia
MRI brain with thin cuts through the posterior fossa and basal ganglia
Genetic testing for myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DMPK CTG repeat expansion)
Nerve conduction studies and electromyography (looking for myotonic discharges)
Trial of levodopa-carbidopa 25/100 mg to assess clinical response

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Functional neurological symptom disorder (functional gait disorder with functional inability to lower the arms)

Alternatives:
1. Frontal gait disorder of normal pressure hydrocephalus (against: no magnetic gait, no urinary incontinence, no cognitive deficit demonstrated)
2. Spinocerebellar ataxia (against: normal coordination exam, no family history obtained, normal posterior fossa on MRI)
3. Dorsal column/posterior column disease such as vitamin B12 deficiency (against: no sensory level, no Romberg reported, normal coordination)
